- Model consistently overestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral; apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is persistently negative (avg < -0.5) over last 5 days, reduce forecast mean by 2–4% to account for mean reversion.
- If forecast is >5% above recent 7-day average, flag for “overshoot” and reduce by 1–3% for next 3 days unless event-driven.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp drop after 10–15 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5 days to reflect lagged reaction.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak (e.g., +0.5+), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from forecast in first 3 days, assume model is “overconfident” and apply 1–2% downward adjustment for remaining horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows “double dip” (peak then drop), reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days to avoid overestimating recovery.
